name: Swiss Ball Knees-to-Chest Push-Up
description: A dynamic push-up variation where the feet rest on a swiss ball and each repetition is paired with a knee tuck that rolls the ball toward the chest. The push-up phase loads the pectoralis major and triceps while the knee tuck activates the hip flexors and rectus abdominis in a compound, full-body movement. The alternating push-and-tuck pattern creates a unique time-under-tension pattern and high core demand.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a push-up plank with shins/feet resting on top of a swiss ball, hands on the floor. Body forms a straight line.
execution.setup_instructions: Fully inflate the ball. Place the ball directly behind and position shins on top. Ensure non-slip floor surface. The ball should be directly under the lower legs at the start.
steps: Step 1: Establish the plank position with shins on the ball, hands shoulder-width on floor.
Step 2: Perform a push-up: lower the chest toward the floor.
Step 3: As you press back up, simultaneously tuck the knees toward the chest by rolling the ball forward.
Step 4: At the top of the push-up, knees are tucked and ball is near the hands.
Step 5: Extend the legs back out, rolling the ball to the start. That is one rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent, exhale as you press and tuck simultaneously.
common_mistakes: Tucking the knees before completing the push-up — the two movements should be coordinated
Ball rolling sideways due to uneven pressure from the feet
Hips rising too high during the tuck, reducing the push-up challenge
safety_considerations: Master swiss ball plank and standard swiss ball push-ups before adding the tuck
Start with partial knee tucks until coordination is established
Ensure ball is fully inflated and on a non-slip surface
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full push-up depth and full knee tuck — knees near the chest at the top of the press.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2-0-2-1 (2s down, coordinated press and tuck, 1s reset)
coaching_cues: Press and tuck at the same time — they happen together
Roll the ball with control — the hip flexors drive the tuck, the chest drives the press
